title: UN General Assembly adopts resolution ES-11/1 deploring Russia's aggression against Ukraine
body:
On 2 March 2022, the United Nations General Assembly adopted resolution ES-11/1, titled "Aggression against Ukraine", at the continuation of its 11th Emergency Special Session. The session was convened after a draft Security Council resolution on the invasion was vetoed on 25 February 2022, the day after Russia's invasion began. The resolution was sponsored by 96 countries.

The vote was 141 in favour, 5 against and 35 abstentions, with 12 member states absent out of 193. The five countries that voted against were Belarus, Eritrea, North Korea, Russia and Syria. Notable abstentions included China, India, Iran, Iraq, Pakistan, South Africa, Kazakhstan, Cuba and Vietnam. The absent states were Azerbaijan, Burkina Faso, Cameroon, Ethiopia, Eswatini, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Morocco, Togo, Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan and Venezuela. Venezuela had been suspended from voting because of unpaid dues.

The resolution deplored Russia's invasion of Ukraine and demanded a full withdrawal of Russian forces. It also demanded that Russia reverse its recognition of the self-declared Donetsk and Luhansk People's Republics. A separate paragraph deplored the involvement of Belarus in the unlawful use of force against Ukraine and urged it to meet its international obligations. General Assembly resolutions are not legally binding, unlike those of the Security Council.
